record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can one show that proving CL ⊆ P would already provide strong evidence that ZPP ⊆ P?

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Show that CL ⊆ P would give strong evidence ZPP ⊆ P.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall the following complexity classes.

- P is the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine running in time polynomial in the input length.
- ZPP (zero-error probabilistic polynomial time) is the class of languages decided by a probabilistic Turing machine that always outputs the correct answer and whose expected running time is polynomial in the input length.
- CL (catalytic logspace) is the class of languages decided by deterministic Turing machines equipped with: (i) a read-only input tape, (ii) a work tape of size O(log n), and (iii) an auxiliary "catalytic" tape of size 2^{O(log n)} = poly(n) that is initialized with an arbitrary string and must be restored to its original content at the end of every computation, with the machine required to halt and output the correct answer on every input regardless of the initial content of the catalytic tape.

Establish a formal connection of the following form: prove that the containment CL ⊆ P would imply strong evidence that ZPP ⊆ P. More precisely, exhibit a theorem showing that if CL ⊆ P holds, then either ZPP = P, or ZPP ⊆ P follows under widely believed hypotheses, or some standard derandomization-style consequence (such as the existence of pseudorandom generators sufficient to derandomize ZPP) follows from CL ⊆ P.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a recent survey on catalytic/space-reuse computation. No published resolution showing that CL ⊆ P implies (evidence for) ZPP ⊆ P appears to exist; recent work on catalytic computation continues to treat the relationship between CL and randomized classes like ZPP/BPP as open.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on catalytic logspace (CL), including the question of whether CL ⊆ P would give strong evidence that ZPP ⊆ P.
